Vanessa —

Thanks for the call earlier. Attached are our first-pass redlines to Redwood's DPA (file: TheraSys_DPA_redline_v1.pdf) and a short SCCs execution checklist. High level: we need a clearer delegation ladder for processor/subprocessor roles, and we have EU transfer concerns (TheraSys stores some customer records in an Azure EU region but may need US processing for analytics).

Key asks:
- Please confirm whether Redwood can accept our proposed carveout language for controller-controller/subprocessor details (see redline p.3).
- Can you provide the standard audit evidence for cross-border transfers (SOC2 scope, KMS details) and the list of subprocessor locations?
- We may need an explicit Transfer Impact Addendum if transfer to non-EEA is required; are you open to that?

Proposed timeline: legal review this week, finalize DPA next week — customer procurement needs execution by 31 May.

Appreciate a quick confirmation on ownership of these asks so I can coordinate with Procurement.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Lin
Head of Procurement — TheraSys Health Inc.

Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 08:46:00 +0000
Subject: Re: DPA redlines + initial SCCs questions

Vanessa / Sarah —

I reviewed the redlines (thanks for sending). High level observations and proposed fixes below — I'm pasting the suggested DPA snippets as inline comments for ease of tracking.

1) Roles: we should keep the DPA language that Redwood is a processor (we are not taking controller obligations). For clarity I propose replacing the redline at p.3 with: "Supplier (Redwood) acts as processor when processing Customer Personal Data on the Customer's behalf; Supplier will only process under documented instructions and will flow down obligations to subprocessors by contract." This avoids making Redwood a joint controller for product telemetry.

2) SCCs: we can execute the EU Commission standard contractual clauses (processor-to-controller or processor-to-processor depending on your flow). If you need a Transfer Impact Addendum, we can accept a limited TIA that lists data categories and destination countries, plus compensating technical safeguards (encryption at rest/in transit, CMK usage). Please confirm the SMETA: which data categories require US processing (PII vs analytics-only aggregates).

3) Subprocessors & Audit Evidence: we'll provide a subprocessor inventory snapshot and a SOC 2 Type II redacted report. For KMS, we can provide a whitepaper describing the CMK flow and an operations contact for advanced questions.

4) Liability / Indemnities: your redline expands controller liabilities into processor scope; we need to propose a middle ground (cap tied to order form value, carveouts for regulatory fines where applicable). Happy to propose specific language if you send the clause numbers you want changed.

Next steps (proposed):
- Sarah: send a short table that maps the data categories and the processing location (EU-only, EU->US, other). That will let us decide whether a TIA is required and scope it.
- Laura & I will produce a marked-up DPA with tracked changes by Mon (24 May).
- Ben / Vanessa: if procurement timeline is hard (31 May), flag now and we can prioritize an exec-level exceptions lane.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min call if helpful.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Data Protection — Redwood Inference
From: Legal <legal@therasys.health>

Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 10:11:00 +0000
Subject: Re: DPA redlines + initial SCCs questions

Karthik / Vanessa —

Thanks for the quick read. Attached is a short processing-location table (TheraSys_processing_map.xlsx) — summary below:
- Customer PII (IDs, contact data): initial collection in EU, enrichment/analytics in US for model training; retention < 3 years.
- Clinical telemetry (de-identified): stored in EU, occasional aggregated exports for global analytics.

We are open to a scoped TIA limited to "PII enrichment/training" datasets only. Our primary concern is auditability and that Redwood's subprocessors do not export to non-approved jurisdictions without notice.

On liability: we can accept a mutual cap for direct damages but need carveouts for regulatory fines where applicable.

We are available for a call Tue 25 May 09:00–12:00 UTC to finalize the scope. Can Redwood confirm a 30-min slot and who will join (privacy + contracts)?

Regards,
TheraSys Legal (on behalf of Sarah Lin)
